question: How do motorist and cyclist deaths compare year by year in NYC, 2013 to 2025?

options.metric: Annual number of motorist deaths and annual number of cyclist deaths, each calculated as the sum of the corresponding killed-person column
options.denominator: No rate denominator; the metric is a sum over crash records in each calendar year
options.grouping: Calendar year and road-user category: motorist or cyclist
options.reason: Annual counts directly compare how many recorded deaths occurred in each road-user category.
options.answer: Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths in every year, ranging from 72–139 motorist deaths and 10–31 cyclist deaths annually; motorist deaths peaked in 2020 and cyclist deaths peaked in 2019 and 2023.
options.interpretation: This framing answers the question for deaths recorded in police-reported NYC motor-vehicle crashes: each plotted value is the annual sum of the motorist- or cyclist-killed column for crashes dated in that calendar year, 2013–2025. Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths in all 13 years; motorist counts ranged from 72 (2016) to 139 (2020), and cyclist counts from 10 (2018) to 31 (2019 and 2023). This directly compares absolute recorded counts but does not measure per-traveler risk or deaths outside these crash records. answer:
1. Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths in every year from 2013–2025: motorist counts ranged from 72 to 139, while cyclist counts ranged from 10 to 31.
2. Motorists accounted for 72.6%–90.9% of recorded motorist-and-cyclist deaths each year, while cyclists accounted for 9.1%–27.4%; the cyclist share was highest in 2019.
